title: Coefficient control and monomial survival in completed monoid hypersurfaces
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local commutative integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], complete and separated for the powers of $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $T$ be a finitely generated additive submonoid of a free abelian group $H$ of finite rank, and let $W:H\to\mathbf Z$ be a homomorphism positive on $T\setminus\{0\}$. Write $A[T]$ for finite sums $\sum_{u\in T}a_u z^u$, with $z^uz^v=z^{u+v}$, and let $B$ be its completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] at $(\mathfrak m,z^u\ (u\ne0))$. Then $B$ is Noetherian and identifies as an $A$-algebra with all coefficient families $(a_u)_{u\in T}$, with componentwise addition and finite convolution
$$(ab)_u=\sum_{v+w=u}a_vb_w.$$
Under this identification $a z^u$ has coefficient $a$ at $u$ and zero elsewhere, so every $z^u$ is nonzero. Suppose $r\in\mathfrak m\setminus\{0\}$ and $\theta\in B$ has constant coefficient $r$. Then $B/(\theta)$ is Noetherian and the image of every $z^u$ is nonzero, including $u=0$. More precisely, for any $u\in T$ and $b\in B$ such that $(\theta b)_v=0$ for all $v$ with $W(v)<W(u)$, one has $b_v=0$ for all those $v$ and $(\theta b)_u=r b_u$. These assertions allow $T=\{0\}$.

proof.text: Choose nonzero additive generators $g_1,\ldots,g_s$ of $T$, allowing $s=0$. The $A$-algebra map $A[X_1,\ldots,X_s]\to A[T]$, $X_i\mapsto z^{g_i}$, is surjective: every $z^u$ is the image of a product of the $X_i$, and finite sums lift term by term. Thus $A[T]$ is of finite type over the Noetherian ring $A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], then [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] to the ideal $J=(\mathfrak m,z^u:u\ne0)$. This proves that $B$ is Noetherian.

Apply [lem-trf-monoid-completion-coefficients] with $P=T$, $G=H$, $w=W$ and $\mathfrak b=J$. The hypotheses are exactly the given Noetherian locality, completeness and separatedness of $A$, finite generation and lattice embedding of $T$, and positivity of $W$. It identifies $B$ as an $A$-algebra with all coefficient families, gives finite convolution and sends $az^u$ to the family supported at $u$ with coefficient $a$. In particular $z^u\ne0$ because its $u$-coefficient is $1\ne0$ in the integral domain $A$.

Fix $u$ and put $N=W(u)\ge0$. Suppose $(	heta b)_v=0$ whenever $W(v)<N$. Strong induction on the nonnegative integer $n<N$ proves $b_v=0$ for every $v$ with $W(v)=n$. In the finite convolution at such a $v$, the summand with first exponent $0$ is $r b_v$. Every other summand has first exponent $a
e0$ and second exponent $c$ with $a+c=v$, hence $0\le W(c)=n-W(a)<n$; it vanishes by induction. Thus $0=(	heta b)_v=r b_v$, and $r

proof.text: In the convolution at $u$, a summand with first exponent $a\ne0$ has second exponent $c$ of weight $W(u)-W(a)<N$, so its $b_c$ vanishes by Step 3. The remaining summand is $\theta_0 b_u=r b_u$. Therefore $(\theta b)_u=r b_u$, including when $N=0$.

source.place: Agent-written coefficient calculation for the refinement of VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70.

proof.text: The canonical map $B\to B/(\theta)$ is a surjective homomorphism, so [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian] and Step 1 make its quotient Noetherian. If the image of some $z^u$ were zero, then $z^u\in(\theta)$, so $z^u=\theta b$ for some $b\in B$: finite sums of multiples of the single generator combine into one multiple. Step 2 gives zero coefficients below $W(u)$ and coefficient $1$ at $u$. Steps 3--4 then give $1=r b_u$. Since $r\in\mathfrak m$, this puts $1$ in the proper maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, a contradiction. Thus every monomial survives.

source.place: Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), quotient argument; agent-written monomial contradiction for ILO VI 1.6(ii).

proof.text: When $T=\{0\}$, the generator list in Step 1 is empty and $A[T]=A$. Step 2 identifies $B$ with $A$, and $\theta=r$. Steps 3--4 have no lower-weight coefficients and say $(rb)_0=rb_0$. Step 5 proves that $1$ survives in $A/(r)$ since $r\in\mathfrak m$. Hence none of the arguments excludes the trivial monoid or the exponent $u=0$.
